functions: iw6mp64_MSStore_ship 14054ACD0 IN_Init; IN_MouseMove (inlined in IN_Frame 14054A790); new: IN_StartRawInput, IN_RawInputAdd, IN_TakeRawMouse (enhanced/win32/win_rawinput.cpp)
description: The mouse aims with raw input only: a thread with a message-only window registered for the mouse (RIDEV_INPUTSINK) adds every relative report, in device counts, to 64-bit counters; IN_MouseMove hands CL_MouseEvent exactly those counts each frame instead of the cursor's movement. No Windows pointer speed or acceleration, no per-frame clamp, no other mouse mode; absolute reports (tablets, remote desktop) are ignored; movement made in the background and on the frame focus returns is dropped. The cursor is still read for the menus and kept in the window. Fixes B0010, B0011.

functions: iw6mp64_MSStore_ship 14030DC20 CL_MouseMove; 14030D4A0 sub_14030D4A0; 14030D3C0 CL_GetMouseMovement; new dvars m_sens, m_invertPitch (registered from IN_Init)
description: Aim in MW2019 units: one count turns the view by m_sens * 0.0066 degrees (m_sens default 1.5, archived), at any field of view, hip fire and ADS alike: no cgameFOVSensitivityScale, cl_mouseAccel, m_filter, m_yaw or m_pitch. View angles are kept in double precision across frames (re-read when something else moves the view); the game's own yaw/pitch speed limits still apply; m_invertPitch inverts vertical look. Fixes B0023.

functions: iw6mp64_MSStore_ship 14062F420 R_CreateDevice; 140631A80 R_RecoverLostDevice (with the R_ResetDevice it inlines); 140675C50 RB_SwapBuffers; import CreateDXGIFactory (enhanced/gfx_d3d/r_init.cpp)
description: Flip-model presentation: the swap chain is DXGI_SWAP_EFFECT_FLIP_DISCARD with two buffers (Windows can then hand the game's buffers straight to the display: independent flip, in fullscreen and in a borderless window covering the monitor), from a DXGI 1.1 factory (CreateDXGIFactory1). Tearing is allowed when IDXGIFactory5 reports support, and a windowed present with r_vsync 0 tears (uncapped or VRR). The device queues at most one frame (IDXGIDevice1::SetMaximumFrameLatency(1)). Flip model unbinds the back buffer at Present, so the render targets bound before it are bound again after it. A lost device's new swap chain is made the same way, after ClearState and Flush (one flip-model swap chain per window). A system that refuses a flip-model swap chain gets the original one. Not yet: the frame-latency waitable object and reading input right after it (needs the frame loop mapped).
